name: Lat Pulldown
description: The lat pulldown is a cable-based vertical pulling exercise that trains the latissimus dorsi and upper back. It is functionally similar to the pull-up but allows precise load adjustment, making it accessible to beginners and useful for high-repetition back training. It is one of the most effective machine-based exercises for developing back width.

execution.starting_position: Sit at the lat pulldown machine with thighs secured under the pads. Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder width with a pronated grip. Arms extended above, slight backward lean from the hips.
execution.setup_instructions: Adjust the knee pad height to firmly secure the thighs. Select an appropriate weight. A slight rearward torso angle of 10–15 degrees is normal.
steps: Depress the shoulder blades and initiate the pull by driving the elbows down toward the floor.
Pull the bar to the upper chest, squeezing the lats hard at the bottom position.
Control the bar back to the starting position with fully extended arms.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale as you pull the bar down. Inhale as you return it.
common_mistakes: Pulling the bar behind the neck, which stresses the cervical spine
Leaning excessively backward, turning it into a rowing movement
Not achieving full arm extension at the top
safety_considerations: Always pull to the front of the body — never behind the neck
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full arm extension at the top, bar to upper chest at the bottom.
coaching_cues: Put your shoulder blades in your back pockets as you pull
Think about pulling your elbows to your hips
